question.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|2y+3|=2y+3,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2y+3| & =9 \\ 2y+3 & =9 \\ 2y & =6 \\ \frac{2y}{2} & =\frac{6}{2} \\ y & =3\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|2y+3|=-(2y+3),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2y+3| & =9 \\ -(2y+3) & =9 \\ -2y-3 & =9 \\ -2y & =12 \\ \frac{-2y}{-2} & =\frac{12}{-2} \\ y & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $y=-6$ and $y=3.$
